理论设计笔记，2026-09-23。本页只讨论模型与思路，尚未实现，也没有数值验: Theory design notes, 2026-09-23. This page discusses only the model and the reasoning; nothing has been implemented or numerically validated yet. Defect excited states are not considered, so the Huang–Rhys model is not used; only the ground state and static response are examined. Long equations and figures scroll horizontally.

Its inverse \(\Phi^{-1}\) is the static compliance; its range \(\ell_{\mathrm{ph}}\) satisfies \(\cosh(1/\ell_{\mathrm{ph}})=1+K_0/2K\), and \(\ell_{\mathrm{ph}}\approx\sqrt{K/K_0}\) for \(K\gg K_0\).
在 Einstein 模型里，缺陷点的振子与其他声子完全不耦合。所谓“局域声子态: In the Einstein model the oscillator at the defect is not coupled to any other phonon. A "local phonon state" then just means one frequency changed by hand: there is no distinction between a local mode and a continuum, no localization length, no resonance, and the phonon local density of states at the defect is always a \(\delta\) function.
加上近邻弹簧 \\(K\\) 之后，才有局域振动模、带隙模（gap mode）和: Only after adding the neighbour springs \(K\) do local vibrational modes, gap modes and resonant modes appear.
色散还消除了 Einstein 声子的一个简并：“被俘获的电子加上远处任意格点的: Dispersion also removes a degeneracy of Einstein phonons: the states "trapped electron plus one phonon on any distant site" all have exactly the same energy in the Einstein model.
\\(K_0\\gt0\\) 让声子带底有能隙，这同样必要。它保证变软或变重的缺: \(K_0\gt0\) opens a gap at the bottom of the phonon band, and this is equally necessary. It guarantees that a softer or heavier defect produces a genuinely localized gap mode, the kind of mode most relevant to trapping. In an acoustic chain (\(K_0=0\)) such defects give only in-band resonances.

刚度变软（固定 \\(\\alpha\\) 和 \\(M\\)）会加深陷阱。: A softer stiffness (at fixed \(\alpha\) and \(M\)) deepens the trap.
质量变重（同位素）带来的“软化”在静态上不加深陷阱，只有非绝热修正。: The "softening" from a heavier mass (an isotope) does not deepen the trap statically; it enters only through non-adiabatic corrections.
所以声子一侧需要两个独立参数：刚度决定静态效应，质量决定动力学效应。: The phonon side therefore needs two independent parameters: the stiffness controls static effects and the mass controls dynamical ones.

This is where the Huang–Rhys model naturally applies; this page stays with the ground state.
（\\(E_{\\mathrm{bind}}\\sim\\omega_{\\ma: (\(E_{\mathrm{bind}}\sim\omega_{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\xi_e\sim\xi_{\mathrm{ph}}\sim1\)): the electron and the local mode form a "molecule". The electron-induced softening and the isotope effect are expected to be largest here: inside the Born–Oppenheimer regime the softening decreases as the trap deepens, while for shallower traps the Born–Oppenheimer approximation itself fails. The three changes are most strongly entangled here, which makes this regime the most worth studying.
